Need to resolve the existing logs.
@amithash@meta.com Why are we not doing this in dbus sensors?

These are GPIO from the CPU directly and not anything that can be recorded with dbus-sensors.  Ideally we will always have a dbus-sensor threshold trigger first, but if the CPU gets really hot it goes into a self-protect state and it raises this GPIO.

You might want to > the command to a temp file 
```
/usr/bin/log-create xyz.openbmc_project.State.Thermal.DeviceOverOperatingTemperature --json "{\"DETECTOR_NAME\": \"/xyz/openbmc_project/state/thermal/%i\"}" > /tmp/prochot_log
```
Done
Might need to store the log path.
Done

```
log-resolve -p $(</tmp/prochot_log) && rm /tmp/prochot_log && if [ ! -e /tmp/thermtrip_log ]; then /usr/bin/log-create xyz.openbmc_project.State.Thermal.DeviceOperatingNormalTemperature --json "{\"DETECTOR_NAME\": \"/xyz/openbmc_project/state/thermal/%i\"}" fi
```
Not sure how much of that garbage I typed can be done in a unit file. Might be better to pass it on to a script?
Done
Might have to do the same thing as prochot.
Done
I dont think this is prochot? You might need a whole new config to handle cpu0-prochot-alert

`cpu0-prochot-alert` is renamed to `irq-cpu-hsc-oc-n` in https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/openbmc/+/77956

That's why I went ahead with this.
